title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (plus at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.74468085106383%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap-percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile the preregistered natural-language attacker-oriented hypothesis with the registered formal estimand, document per-condition pipeline semantics with explicit archived-artifact references (shared_initial_candidate reuse), disclose the protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature in execution/model_configuration.json), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts cited in Methods and Results.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) offer operational efficiency in network operations (NetOps) by translating high-level operator intent to device CLI. However, LLM outputs can contain syntax, ordering, and semantic errors and are vulnerable to adversarially crafted inputs and prompt-injection, raising operational safety concerns. Prior prototype work shows that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and localized repair reduces errors at prototype scale [1–4]. Yet evaluation practices often rely on token- or reference-match metrics rather than deployability or encoded safety properties. This study asks a focused operational question and tests it within a preregistered confirmatory framework: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? We preregistered study cand-2026-03 and executed the frozen plan with shared_initial_candidate semantics so that, for each adversarial intent, a single initial LLM generation was produced and evaluated under both Baseline and Guarded scoring paths. The manuscript contributes: (1) a preregistered paired experiment with archived execution and analysis artifacts; (2) artifact-grounded quantitative results showing a small but statistically detectable absolute change in deterministic-validator acceptance for the guarded pipeline on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank; and (3) reconciliations requested by reviewers (formal vs natural-language hypothesis, explicit per-condition pipeline timeline with artifact references, and an explicit disclosure of an unset sampling temperature recorded in execution/model_configuration.json).
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification tools such as Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber and VeriFlow offer formal checks for forwarding invariants and configuration constraints and are commonly used as validators in research on automated configuration generation [5–7]. Empirical NetOps investigations demonstrate that LLMs can generate useful configuration drafts but produce syntax/semantic mistakes; tool-assisted generate–validate–repair architectures improve outcomes in prototype settings [2,3,8]. Surveys of AIOps and telecommunications highlight fragmented evaluation metrics and call for operationally meaningful benchmarks emphasizing deployability and safety rather than lexical matches [4,9]. Security analyses document prompt-injection and indirect attack vectors that motivate input-sanitization and gating defenses for LLM-integrated applications [10]. Tool-augmented orchestration research (e.g., Toolformer-style approaches) illustrates practical patterns where LLMs call external checks and then repair outputs based on verifier feedback [11]. Our experiment differs by preregistering a single paired formal estimand that operationalizes acceptance-for-deployment by a deterministic validator, using shared_initial_candidate semantics so paired comparisons isolate downstream processing (sanitization, gating, repair), and publishing per-episode validator traces to make principal numbers traceable to archived artifacts.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. For each adversarial intent the binary outcome equals 1 if the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; 95% bootstrap-percentile CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 (recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Design, task bank and scope. The preregistration specified N = 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300 across two conditions). The synthetic intent templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU/VLAN operations, safe-ordering patterns and constrained required sequences. The adversary model comprises deterministic mutation heuristics of the templates; generation seeds and the mutation taxonomy appear in execution/task_manifest.jsonl. Scope is explicitly limited to synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar used by the validator; no private production data was used.

Model, validator, orchestration and declared runtime. The archived run declares declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 in execution/model_configuration.json (path recorded in the manifest). Orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Provider-call accounting and orchestration stage semantics are recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution/execution_manifest.json. Protocol deviation: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); we disclose this unset sampling parameter as a protocol deviation and preserve paired comparability via shared_initial_candidate semantics (detailed below).

Per-condition pipeline timeline and artifact-grounded semantics. To resolve reviewer-requested clarity, we explicitly enumerate per-condition steps and give representative archived-artifact pointers that demonstrate how shared_initial_generation and downstream processing were executed:
1) Task instantiation and adversarial mutation are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (example: task-000001 task_manifest entry). The task payload includes the intent, required_sequence, constraints and generation_seed (see representative task entries in the archived manifest).
2) Shared initial generation: a single LLM call produced a shared_initial_candidate saved at execution/responses/task-<id>-shared-initial.txt and referenced by both condition scoring records. Evidence: stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json), and execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json both reference the same shared_initial_candidate SHA-256 and shared_initial_response_path.
3) Baseline scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 evaluated the shared_initial_candidate and produced the baseline decision recorded in execution/scoring/<...>-baseline.json (validation_before/validation_after and final_state are present there).
4) Guarded branch: the pipeline applied template-based input-sanitization prior to the verifier gate (sanitizer outputs are recorded in task_manifest payload fields when changes occur), then the verifier-gate evaluated the candidate; if allowed by gating policy, at-most-one automated repair LLM call was permitted. Repair invocations and traces are present in provider-call traces and in execution/scoring/<...>-guarded.json where repair_applied, repair_prompt_sha256 and repair traces appear. Analysis artifact stage_counts.repair = 6 documents the number of repair-stage calls (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
5) Final validation: the validator re-evaluated any repaired candidate and recorded the guarded final decision and validator trace (execution/scoring/<...>-guarded.json files include validation_before/validation_after snapshots and violation lists). Representative artifacts: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt, execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json, execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.

Missingness, exclusions and treatment of technical failures. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. The archive records completed_episodes = 282, failed_episodes = 18, and complete_pairs_used = 141 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Provider-call accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed = 147, failed = 9, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6; these counts validate that repair calls occurred only in a small subset of episodes.
sections.results:
Execution and aggregated counts. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model provider calls used = 156 (execution/execution_manifest.json). The primary confirmatory analysis used 141 complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline_successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085106383); guarded_successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01 = 0, n00 = 0.

Statistical inference. The exact two-sided McNemar test on the observed paired outcomes yields p = 0.03125 (primary confirmatory test). The point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Bootstrap-percentile 95% CI using 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]; bootstrap parameters and log entries are in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. These numeric values are reproduced directly from analysis/results.json and analysis artifacts archived with the run.

Discordant-case diagnostics and repair association. The six discordant n10 pairs are traceable to repair-stage activity: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json reports repair calls = 6 and provider-call stage_counts indicate repair = 6. Per-episode scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-<id>-guarded.json) contain validator validation_before/validation_after snapshots showing that sanitization and/or permitted repair changed command ordering or normalization such that deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted the final guarded candidate whereas the unguarded baseline candidate failed. Representative artifact triplet for one discordant case: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt, execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json, execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (all archived and referenced in the manifest).

Missingness sensitivity. Nine pairs were both-run technical failures and excluded per the preregistered plan (analysis/missingness_summary.csv: both_missing_pairs = 9). Under a conservative sensitivity that treats both-missing pairs as failures, baseline acceptance becomes 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance 141/150 = 0.9400. The preregistered primary inference uses only the 141 complete pairs and the observed discordant set (n10 = 6, n01 = 0); the reported p-value 0.03125 reproduces from the archived paired contingency.

Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in the archived run; the absence of those artifacts is visible in the execution manifest and task directories. Consequently, this run does not provide empirical false-positive-blocking rates and we make no claims about benign-input blocking.
sections.discussion:
Reconciliation of preregistered wording and the formal estimand. The preregistration natural-language H1 stated that verifier-gating would reduce attacker-success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The registered formal estimand measured paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These are distinct: an increase in validator acceptance can reflect successful repair of malformed drafts (reducing operator labor) rather than enabling attacker success. Observed data show guarded acceptance > baseline (an absolute increase ≈ 4.255 percentage points) because sanitizer/repair recovered reparable drafts that the baseline validator rejected. Thus the preregistered natural-language attacker-centric claim is not supported by the formal-estimand outcome; we report and interpret the formal-estimand result and caution against conflating validator acceptance with attacker-centric safety without an independent semantic-safety oracle.

Operational implications, repair–gate co-design and failure modes. Within this controlled synthetic setting, template-based sanitization combined with a conservative verifier-gate and a restrained repair policy recovered valid, deployable configurations that unguarded generation failed to produce. The six discordant pairs exemplify a trade-off: repairs enabled acceptance but—under weaker validator encodings—could permit semantically unsafe outputs. Thus operational deployment requires co-design: (i) gate rules that conservatively express the safety invariants of interest, (ii) limited repair scopes with explicit guardrails, and (iii) an independent semantic-safety oracle (e.g., dynamic reachability checks) when possible.

Threats to validity and generalizability. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size and triggered the preregistered exclusion rule (both-run failures = 9). Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes CLI grammar, required sequences and protected-interface invariants but omits some protocol-level dynamic semantics; acceptance-for-deployment is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator and synthetic intents limit generalization across vendors, protocols and production topologies. Conclusion validity: observed absolute effect is small against a high baseline acceptance (ceiling effect); detectability does not imply wide practical impact.

Protocol deviation, paired comparability, and reproducibility. The archived execution/model_configuration.json recorded temperature = null (unset). We treat this as a protocol deviation because provider defaults may affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single generation per pair). Artifact evidence confirming this pattern includes stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 and the per-episode shared_initial_candidate files referenced by both baseline and guarded scoring artifacts (see execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json). For deterministic reproduction, future runs should set temperature = 0 explicitly and re-execute the archived task manifest under identical provider semantics.

Recommendations grounded in archived evidence. Immediate next steps supported by the archived artifacts: (1) execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking; (2) preregister and evaluate an attacker-centric estimand that couples validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle or operational reachability checks; (3) diversify generator and validator implementations across vendors and CLI dialects; and (4) fix sampling settings (temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction. Each recommendation follows directly from observed artifacts and provider-call accounting in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]). Per-episode validator traces and reconciliation stage_counts indicate the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. Crucially, this formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker-centric success under attacker definitions; an independent semantic-safety oracle is required to claim lowered attacker success. Limitations include synthetic scope, single model/validator evaluation, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent oracle, diversify models/validators, and set explicit sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results (artifact paths cited in the paper).

limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
